The Deep Intelligence Money
by Hetu Pod
October 1, 2025
Abstract
The abundance economy is coming. Liquidity is imbued with trust-minimization, and produc￾tivity is accelerated by deep intelligence. As the marginal cost of intelligence is asymptotically
approaching zero, the shift of this agentic economy needs to be rebalanced by native money and
p2p payment and financing systems. Hetu invents a native money protocol turning intelligence
into a decentralized digital good, by pricing data, compute, models, post-training, and agents by
tracking their causal contribution to useful outcomes. Peers emit verifiable events that form a
causal DAG; a DAG-local Shapley approximation algorithmically routes credit for each contri￾bution and settles on a high-throughput DAG ledger with an EVM layer. The system utilizes
peer-to-peer reinforcement learning to generate per-request routing receipts, which aggregate to
form dynamic market weights. This ensures that payments are precisely targeted to providers
who improve utility. The network’s integrity is further reinforced by incentives that couple stake￾weighted attention with verifiability, rendering malicious collusion economically irrational. This
process is secured by Proof of Causal Work (PoCW), a novel, intersubjective consensus mechanism
that validates the process of how a result was achieved, rather than the final output itself. The
protocol’s economy is built on two pillars: a native currency ($HETU) with an issuance governed
by a predictable logarithmic decay that increasingly shifts incentives toward specialized subnets,
and using proven contributions a meritbased, nontransferable Flux balances – Intelligence Native
Money – redeemable oneway into AI stablecoins, yielding a market that continuously discovers,
routes, and pays for verifiable capability.
1 Introduction
Hetu introduces the concept of Intelligence Money. Contributions that are proven useful by PoCW
mine nontransferable Flux balancesa soulbound, onchain resume of verifiable capabilitythat can
be redeemed oneway into stablecoins via a dedicated liquidity bridge. This preserves merit as the
source of issuance while allowing earned intelligence to fund realworld activity. On top of these
primitives, Hetu supports a suite of applications: a P2P AI payment protocol, autonomous stablecoin
vaults, decentralized training, ModelDAOs for science, cashflow financing for AIs, AI social monies,
and intersubjective AI governance.
Hetu is also a protocol for turning intelligence into a native digital good. It organizes a permissionless market in which data, curation, compute, models, posttraining, and agents are continuously
priced by their causal contribution to useful outcomes across the network. Every upload, training
step, inference, and agent action is emitted as a verifiable event and stitched into a causal DAG; from
this fabric, credit flows forward to the participants who actually moved the needle. In short: produce
measurable utility, prove how it arose, and get paid.
At the core of Hetu’s accounting is causal attribution. Exact counterfactuals are infeasible at
network scale, so Hetu implements a DAG-local Shapley-style approximation that is compositional,
updateable, and resistant to the injection of spurious contributions. Events carry vector-clock [1]
ordering, TEE attestations, and cryptographic receipts tying inputs to outputs; marginal contributions
are computed locally and aggregated along paths to terminals such as evaluation gains, paid inferences,
and completed tasks. This yields raw causal scores that can be settled in near-real time without
requiring any central judgement of “quality.”
This attribution engine also serves as a routing market. Hetu’s decentralized Mixture-of-Experts
(dMoE) gates requests to a sparse set of providers per input, then emits “routing receipts” that quantify
which experts improved utility on that input. Aggregated over an epoch, these receipts form a market
weight matrix that captures who depends on whom. Rewards follow attention, but only when attention
1
is backed by verifiability: peers earn when staked consumers rely on them, when their work is attested
and reproducible, and when they are connected to the honest, stake-reachable giant component rather
than an isolated clique.
Consensus in Hetu is intersubjective rather than absolute. The network does not attempt to agree
on the content of a result; it agrees on the validity of causal histories that lead to results. Proof
of Causal Work (PoCW) establishes an auditable, tamper-evident narrative of cause and effect: a
cryptographically linked sequence of “if-then” events whose structural integrity can be checked inde￾pendently of subjective judgments. This allows heterogeneous communitieshumans, institutions, and
agentsto coordinate on what happened and who contributed, without enforcing a single worldview
about what those events “mean.”
Economic settlement is handled by a highthroughput DAGbased ledger with an EVMcompatible
layer for market logic. The native token, $HETU, is issued on a predictable, logarithmically decaying
schedule and split between a hub and a dynamic set of subnets using a “Logarithmic Subnet Incentive”
model that tilts emissions toward useful horizontal expansion. Onchain value attribution extends the
causal toolkit to economic flows: subnet utilities and moneyflows are transformed into verifiable causal
graphs whose “Causal Flux,” together with TVL, direct rewards and unlock credit products backed
by predictable income.
The remainder of the litepaper develops these pieces in turn. Section 2 defines the peer-to-peer
intelligence market, from event semantics and DAG-Shapley attribution to routing receipts and incen￾tive formation. Section 3 formalizes intersubjective consensus via PoCW. Section 4 details $HETU
issuance, subnet economics, and on-chain value attribution. Section 5 introduces $USDAI as intelli￾gence stable coin. Section 6 introduces an intelligence mined only native money $FLUX. In Section
7 introduces frameworks of alignment andgovernance. Section 8 illustrates different applications that
Hetu protocol directly targets. Section 9 concludes the litepaper.
2 Peer-to-Peer Intelligence Market
Hetu organizes a permissionless market where intelligence – data, curation, compute, models, posttraining, and agents – is continuously priced by its causal contribution to outcomes produced across
the network. Peers emit verifiable events (uploads, jobs, inferences, policy actions) that form a DAG
of causality. From this DAG, Hetu derives who helped whom, by how much, and routes newlymined
rewards and fees toward the most causally useful participants. A decentralized MixtureofExperts
(dMoE) layer turns this into live routing: each request only pays the few peers that actually improved
it.
2.1 Entities and primitives

Events e ∈ E: atomic actions, e.g., publish dataset shard, run training step, serve inference, agent

• Parent references parents(e) to prior events,
• A causal vector clock (CV) proving partial order,
• A TEE attestation a(e) (measurement of code/data, nonce, time),
• Cryptographic receipts (signatures, Merkle proofs) tying inputs to outputs.
Causal DAG G = (E, →): edges respect “happensbefore”; events with no path on DAG are “concurrent”.
Consumers: any peer that issues a request (training step, inference, agent decision) and receives
utility U (e.g., loss decrease, reward, revenue).
Ledger: a highperformance DAGbased blockchain that finalizes event commitments and runs an
EVMcompatible execution layer.

2.4 Incentives: rank, legitimacy, and connectivity
Hetu converts weights and stakes into rank. Let S denote the current stake rector. Attention-based
rank R of a provider is computed as:
R = WT S
This formulation indicates that a provider ranks highly if many staked consumers depend on its
outputs.
Each peer also receives a legitimacy score L ∈ [0, 1]. This score is derived from TEE attestations,
reproducibility proofs, and DAG-consistency checks (no broken provenance, no unverifiable data use).
Illegitimate or unverifiable work cannot turn attention into rewards.
Next, to resist collusion, Hetu measures how embedded a peer is within the stake-reachable portion

2.5 Fees, slashing, and identity
Consumers pay a fee with each receipt. These fees are then split across the selected experts in proportion to Wk,∗.
Successful challenges reduce the legitimacy score L of the peer. They also trigger TEE replays,
and will slash bonded stakes. New peers join by posting a TEE registration and a minimal bond. The
network does not maintain a whitelist and is open to all participants.
3 Intersubjective Consensus
Intersubjective Consensus in our system is not about forcing all peertopeer entities to agree on a
single, objective ”truth.” Instead, it’s about achieving a shared agreement on the validity of causal
histories. This is powered by Proof of Causal Work (PoCW). When an entity acts, PoCW doesn’t ask
the network to validate the content of the action, but rather to verify that the action is a legitimate,
cryptographically-linked consequence of a prior event. This creates a tamper-proof chain of ”if-then”
statementsa verifiable narrative of cause and effect.
PoCW operationalizes this principle for digital interactions by ensuring the integrity of event se￾quences, independent of any agent’s subjective interpretation of those events. As individual entities
construct their respective causal chains, these chains can intersect and reference one another within
the architecture of the Decentralized Knowledge Graph. Intersubjective consensus, therefore, emerges
organically from the increasing density and interconnectedness of these verifiable histories. This pro￾cess cultivates a collective, verifiable understanding of the system’s evolution, one that is grounded in
provable relationships rather than reliance on a central authority or brute-force computation.
PoCW Formal Structure
The continuous exchange of vector clocks builds a graph structure of events in a peer-to-peer network
structure. Since each entity in such a network has its own view that is constantly being synchronized,
this creates a Decentralized Knowledge Graph (DKG). Proof of Causal Work (PoCW) is the verification
process that validates contributions to this DKG. The verification is twofold, separating the structural
integrity of the graph from the qualitative assessment of the work it represents.
The DKG is a directed acyclic graph G = (V, E) where vertices represent events and edges represent
direct causal dependencies.
Vertices (V): Each vertex v ∈ V corresponds to a proofofevent Πe, which is a tuple: Πe = (e, Ce, σe)
• e: The event data, including a payload and type, e.type ∈ {Objective, Subjective}

• Ce: The ndimensional vector clock [t1, t2, . . . , tn] of the executing agent after event e.
• σe: The digital signature of the agent on the hash of the event and its clock,
Sign(privKey, H(e ∥Ce)).

PoCW Verification Function
The Proof of Causal Work (PoCW) is validated by a main function, VerifyPoCW, which confirms
that a new contribution Πnew is valid with respect to the existing graph G. This function is a logical
conjunction of two distinct verification components:
VerifyPoCW(G, Πnew) ≡ Verify Graph(G, Πnew) ∧ Verify Task(Πnew)
Deterministic Graph Verification: Verify Graph
This function checks the structural and cryptographic integrity of a new proof Πnew = (e, Ce, σe). It
must satisfy two conditions:
1. Authentication: The signature must be valid against the agent pi

Where UpdateRule is the deterministic vector clock update logic defined previously. Graph
verification failure may occur at any stage, and consequently, the graph will not be mutated

Task-Dependent Verification: Verify Task
This function’s logic is conditional on the event type e.type.

• If e.type == Subjective: Verification relies on an intersubjective consensus protocol among a set
of designated voting entities, Voters(e).

4 $Hetu, the intelligence fair money
$Hetu is a fully decentralized, community-owned, fair-launched AI Bitcoin, created to balance the
emerging AI economy through intelligence mining. Its governance is purely transparent and trustless,
embodying our vision of intelligence as a shared public good, our mission of enabling communities
to co-create and self-govern, and our values of fairness, openness, and resilience. $Hetu is not just a
token, but a foundation for an AI-native civilization where trust, intelligence, and meaning converge
into a new economic paradigm.
5
4.1 On-Chain Fair Attribution of $HETU
Hetu applies intelligence mining techniques to OnChain Value Attribution (OCVA) and develops
credit products backed by utility audit and predictable income. The core idea: use TVL Tournaments
(subnet competition based on TVL) to direct capital toward highquality subnets, while transforming
subnet utility events and money-flow into auditable causal graphs. Those causal proofs produce a
Causal Flux that, together with TVL, determines subnet reward allocation. Verified, predictable
income derived from the causal model can then be used as collateral to support credit instruments for
subnets.
4.2 Core Concepts
On-Chain Value Attribution (OCVA)
1. TVL Tournaments
• At each settlement epoch, the system measures each subnet’s TVL and allocates the Subnet
Rewards pool according to relative shares.
• Goal: Use capital allocation as a competitive incentive so subnets continuously improve
service, performance, and economic design.
2. Events and money-flow PK
• Inputs: utilities events (API calls, model invocations, paid usage, SLA metrics, unique
users) and money flow (onchain transfers, payments, revenue receipts).
• Processing: Convert events into causalordered verifiable event streams and extract causal
relationships (DAG) using signed logs, Merkle roots, and verifiable computation.
• Output: Flux for each entity, quantifying its contribution to real economic value.
4.3 Tokenomics

dynamically adjusts each block’s reward based on the proportion of issued tokens relative to total

5 $USDAI, The Intelligence Stable Money
$USDAI is an AIdriven stablecoin embedded with a threelayered value flow enhanced by cash flow
financing mechanisms. Its foundation is anchored by USDT /USDC and U.S. Treasuries, protected
by risk isolation mechanisms. Over time, part of its liquidity is redirected into the AI infrastructure
market, with $USDAI further linking datasets, AI models, and intelligent enduser services across the
entire AI ecosystem. By integrating payments and cash flow financing at each layer,$USDAI enables
financial reserves, compute resources, and AI outputs to be efficiently monetized and recycled. This
builds a dynamic closed loop
“Financial Reserves → AI Infrastructure → Intelligent Outputs → Revenue Feedback”
positioning USDAI as the core settlement medium connecting global AI resources, capital, and de￾mand, while overcoming the static peg limitations of traditional stablecoins.
$USDAI is a three-layer AI stablecoin designed to link financial stability with AI ecosystem growth.
Layer One ensures baseline stability through 1:1 collateralization with USDT /USDC, while a portion
of funds generates yield via U.S. Treasuries and high-quality assets. Layer Two channels liquidity into
AI infrastructure through cash flow-based financing, allowing providers to collateralize future income
and expand capacity, forming a dynamic cycle:
“Liquidity → Financing → AI Infrastructure → Exit”
Layer Three integrates payments, collaboration, and financing, enabling seamless cross-border AI
transactions, incentivizing global model and dataset collaboration, and granting holders priority access to funding, creating a unified, selfsustaining AI economic ecosystem.
This completes the growth loop sustained by cash flow financing that maintains growth and liquidity.
“Financial Reserves → AI Infrastructure → Intelligent Outputs → Revenue Feedback”
To support this infrastructure, a largescale Ethereum Layer 2 will anchor $USDAI, consolidating
liquidity into the AI economy. In addition, $BTC, $ETH, and $HETU may serve as collateral to
further power AI infrastructure. The revenue model for $USDAI and its chain derives from gas fees
and commissions generated by AI cash flow financing.
Beyond its core P2P intelligence network, Hetu extends $USDAI into specialized subnet ecosys￾tems. Each subnetwhether for GPU compute, dataset sharing, or vertical model marketsoperates
with $USDAI as its settlement layer, ensuring liquidity, stability, and interoperability. This design
enables subnets to function as autonomous yet interconnected economies: incentivizing contributions,
rewarding collaboration, and enabling frictionless value exchange. Over time, $USDAI will not only
coordinate resources within Hetu but also enable cross-subnet composability, making the entire intel￾ligence network more scalable, resilient, and self-evolving.
6 $Flux, The Intelligence Native Money
Flux is not a conventional tokenit is an intelligent native money designed for the abundance AI
economy. There are threedimensional currencies designed for the age of intelligent systems.
1. Utility cash for intelligence instant payment
Flux functions as liquid cash in AI–human and AI–AI interactions. It can be used directly
for payments, microtransactions, and service exchanges, ensuring real utility as a transactional
medium.
2. Consensus currency for social coordination
Beyond payment, Flux acts as a consensus layer. It directs collective interaction and cooperation,
aligning participantshumans, AIs, and organizationsinto shared economic and cultural flows.
